sources.title: Official NAM RealHighway feature guide
facts: Levels are spaced7.5m; DD lowerL1=7.5m and upperL2=15m.
Ramp families distinguish orthogonal, diagonal, and fractional18.4degree branches. FARHW uses18.4/71.6degree FA3 headings.
MRC radius families are R1,R2,R3,R4,R5, increasing in radius; the reviewed prose does not give exact metre radii.
FLEXHeight includes one/two-level orthogonal/diagonal variants,90degree curved transitions, a one-level MIS180degree loop, and one-level R3 45degree curved transitions.
Ramp-style transitions suit relatively level terrain; on-slope transitions require an embankment.
FLEXRamps are plopped override interfaces; DRIs use drag patterns; fractional C/F ramps require puzzle pieces.
sources.limits: Documented supported native families, not compatibility certification for custom6m pieces; exact native geometry and version50 support need local resource measurement.

sources.title: Official NAM RealHighway compatibility table
facts: MIS45degree R0/R1/R2/R3 are listed supported;R4/R5 have FLEX-or-puzzle-only partial support.
MIS90degree R1 is supported;R2 is FLEX-or-puzzle-only partial support.
MIS straight orthogonal/diagonal height transitions cover listed one/two-level changes.
sources.limits: R labels are family names, not metre radii. Do not infer DDRHW or custom model support from MIS row.

sources.title: Metropolitan Expressway operator: steep tight large-section shield tunnels at Baba entrance/exit
facts: Four urban ramp tunnels face steep grades, tight curves, small cover, and proximity to operating mainline tunnels and important structures.
sources.limits: Reviewed text provides no numerical road radius/grade. Its7.2degree value is shield-machine articulation, NOT road heading or ramp slope. Baba is in Yokohama, not central Tokyo.

sources.title: NEXCO West official FAQ: highway curves

sources.limits: Supports smooth transition inspiration only, not a particular radius or grade for the custom kit.

calculations.basis: Own arithmetic; constant-grade horizontal lower bounds before flat collars or vertical easing. SC4 tile scale16m from project and official NAM guide.

proposal_implications: Use a small declared angle/radius/grade vocabulary for interchangeability; proposed24/40/56m radii are custom kit choices, not official NAM MRC metre equivalents.
Realistic-looking compact urban ramps may draw inspiration from30-35km/h project examples with30-40m radii and approximately8-9percent grades, while still requiring many tiles to lose7.5-15m height.
A two/three-tile high-deck descent must be explicitly classed as game compression, not real-world engineering compliance.
Flat standard ports are recommended for interchangeability but not mathematically required; exact matching sloped ports remain possible.
Do not use a single material slope donor as proof of a generic native FLEXHeight length or slope.
The retained6m custom width is not an automatic native MIS interface.
